structured_output.summary:
The loop has made solid progress. E007 (Muon) is the first feasible run, and the post-mortems are careful. The tree's bookkeeping, though, has fallen behind the evidence:
- H1.4 and H2.2 keep high confidence even though their own children were refuted.
- H1.5's evidence tokens are mis-assigned. E008 actually agrees with H1.5, and E009/E010 test a different claim.
- H1.1.2 is marked "supports" although its stated threshold of >=0.756 was missed.

On the evidence itself:
- The incumbent's lead rests on one run that changed optimizer, batch size and epochs together.
- It clears the local bar by only 0.14 pp, about one seed-sampling sigma.
- The 1 pp/s exchange rate used to judge E009 and E010 was measured under SGD. That is the same transfer error that E008's own post-mortem warns against.
- The claim that the depth cut is twice as efficient as the width cut rests on a difference of under 1 sigma.

The most informative surprise is that removing 6% of the MACs cut step time by 9%, while widening deep layers was almost free. This points to memory-bandwidth-bound high-resolution layers, which contradicts E006's explanation that cuDNN convs dominate. No hypothesis covers this yet.

Several cheap directions are still untested:
- alternating flip, label smoothing and Cutout ablations
- progressive resizing and data filtering
- the Muon epoch slope, and tuning Muon's lr, momentum and batch size
- the Lookahead and BN-bias-LR settings carried over from the SGD setup

The Lvl1 set also leaves out two things: seed variance and safety margin as a lever on the score, and the memory-bound nature of step cost.

critiques.issue: H1.1.2 predicts a rise to >=0.756 for <=12% more time. E002 reached 0.7482, which is 0.8 pp short, and took +12.3% time. Both stated thresholds were missed, yet the verdict is 'supports'. The verdict judges only the delta clause (>=0.4 pp) and ignores the absolute clause.
critiques.suggestion: Re-label E002 as E002~ (or as refuting the absolute-level part) for H1.1.2. When verdicts are pre-registered, every clause of the prediction should be scored, not only the convenient one.

critiques.issue: E003 showed that accuracy is bit-identical across re-runs, so the clause 're-run changes the mean by <=0.2 pp' is vacuously true and says nothing about noise. The noise that matters is the sensitivity to small perturbations. Several runs already show it: E005 changed the RNG stream, E006 changed numerics, and per-seed values moved by up to 0.4 pp with mean shifts of about 0.07 pp. Treating the run-to-run noise as ~0 invites over-reading of small deltas.
critiques.suggestion: Estimate perturbation noise directly. Run the incumbent 2-3 times with only an internal data-order/augmentation salt changed (the trial seeds stay fixed) and use the spread of the 3-seed mean (likely ~0.15-0.2 pp) as the inconclusive band. Mark H1.1.3 as E003~.

critiques.issue: H1.4.1 was refuted, but H1.4 is still 'open' at 0.55. E007 also changed three things at once: optimizer, batch size (1024->2000) and epochs (9.5->9.0). The +0.69 pp lead could partly come from batch 2000, from fewer and larger steps, or from Muon interacting with Lookahead and the 64x BN-bias LR. It is one run at ~2.5 sigma, and it clears 0.753 by only 0.14 pp, about one sigma of the 40-seed vs 3-seed gap.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H1.4 as refuted, or drop its confidence to <=0.2. Ablate SGD at batch 2000 and Muon at batch 1024 to attribute the gain. Treat 0.7544 as marginal and prefer moves that land at >=0.755.

critiques.target: Exchange rate used in E009/E010 verdicts
critiques.issue: The 'about 1 pp per epoch / about 1 pp per second' rate was measured under SGD between 8.5 and 9.5 epochs (E001->E002). E009 and E010 were scored against it under Muon at batch 2000, where the epoch slope has never been measured. E008's post-mortem warns against exactly this kind of transfer from the SGD setting.
critiques.suggestion: Before more trade-off verdicts, measure Muon's epoch slope: the incumbent at 8.5 and 9.5 epochs, or at 8.5 and 10. Re-score E009 and E010 against that slope.

critiques.issue: H1.5 says that 576 in the last group at about 8.5 epochs is near-optimal and that trading width for epochs gains <=5%. E008 (768 is worse under Muon) is consistent with that claim, yet it is tagged as refuting it. E009 and E010 vary group-1 depth and width, which H1.5 does not address, yet they are tagged as supporting it. As a result the node's 0.45 confidence and its evidence string do not mean anything.
critiques.suggestion: Split H1.5 into two hypotheses: an optimizer-conditional group-3 width claim (E004- under SGD, E008+ under Muon) and a new Lvl2 claim that per-step cost concentrates in group 1, so cheapening it beats cutting epochs (E009+, E010+). Fix the tokens to match.

critiques.target: E009 vs E010 conclusion ('depth cut is 2x better than width cut')
critiques.issue: The comparison of 0.41 vs 0.82 pp/s rests on an accuracy difference of 0.18 pp (0.7515 vs 0.7497) between two single runs, and that difference is within the perturbation noise. The follow-up decision ('discard width 96', 'combining both cuts is unlikely to help') is built on a difference inside noise.
critiques.suggestion: Treat E009 vs E010 as inconclusive. If group 1 is the bottleneck, test the combination (2 convs at width 96 or 112) with +epochs before discarding it.

critiques.target: Surprise: E009 (-6% MACs -> -9% step time) and E004 (+19% MACs -> +6%)
critiques.issue: Step time clearly does not track FLOPs, and the cost sits in the 32x32/16x16 layers. That pattern points to memory-bandwidth-bound elementwise work (training-mode BN, activations, pooling, fp16 activation traffic at batch 1024-2000), not to conv math. It contradicts E006's explanation that 'cuDNN convs dominate'. No hypothesis captures this.
critiques.suggestion: Profile one step with torch.profiler and break time down by kernel. Add an H2 Lvl2 node: 'group-1 cost is memory-bound, and fusing or cheapening BN and activations there (compile fusion, a cheaper activation, removing a BN, an earlier pool, a stride-2 whitening) cuts step time more than conv changes do'.

critiques.issue: E006 refuted H2.2.1 (-1.9% vs >=30% predicted), but H2.2 is still at 0.70. Also, fp16 and channels_last were already in E001, so only the compile mode was ever tested and the precision and layout parts were never ablated.
critiques.suggestion: Lower H2.2 to about 0.3 and narrow its claim to the compile mode. If precision and layout are still of interest, test them separately (bf16 vs fp16, channels_last off) using profiler evidence.

critiques.issue: E001 adopted the GPU-resident loader as part of the bundle, so the comparison with the CPU DataLoader can no longer be made on the critical path. The node is open at 0.70 with no evidence and will never be tested in its current form.
critiques.suggestion: Close it as subsumed (adopted in E001, untested) so it stops taking confidence mass, or turn it into a check that augmentation time is under 1% of step time.

critiques.issue: Prepare is now about 0.06 s, and 225 steps × 38.5 ms ≈ 8.66 s, which nearly equals train time, so in-train overhead is small. One sign remains: E007's first trial trains about 0.15 s slower (8.76 vs 8.59/8.61 s), probably a first-call cost of the Muon/Newton-Schulz kernels or the allocator. Otherwise H3 is close to exhausted, yet it stays at 0.50.
critiques.suggestion: Make one targeted fix: warm up the full optimizer step, including Muon, in build, which is worth about 0.05 s on the mean. Then lower H3 to about 0.2 and stop allocating ideas to it.

critiques.target: Never-tested nodes: H1.2, H1.3, H1.6, H2.3
critiques.issue: Alternating flip, label smoothing 0.3, the Cutout hurts claim, data filtering and progressive resizing all have zero experiments. Alternating flip and ls 0.3 are baked into the recipe, unvalidated for CIFAR-100, and were tuned for SGD. The E008 lesson ('re-validate after an optimizer switch') applies here too.
critiques.suggestion: Under Muon, run cheap single-knob ablations: ls 0.2 vs 0.3, random vs alternating flip. Progressive resizing (H2.3) fits the finding that the high-resolution layers are expensive and could pay off well; give it priority over more width tweaks.

critiques.target: Muon hyperparameters and inherited SGD components
critiques.issue: Muon was used at the literature defaults (lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, 3 NS steps, batch 2000) and never tuned. Lookahead, the triangular schedule and the 64x BN-bias LR are all carried over from the SGD setup. E008's alternative explanation (lr not right for 768 width) was never tested either.
critiques.suggestion: Run a small sweep: Muon lr ×{0.7, 1.4}, momentum {0.6, 0.85}, Lookahead on/off, and batch {1500, 2500}. Removing Lookahead under Muon may be a free gain.

critiques.issue: The score depends on how close the recipe can run to the bar, and that is set by per-seed variance: E007's per-seed range is 0.6 pp. No hypothesis treats reducing variance (EMA of weights, a longer final LR anneal, label-smoothing tuning) as a lever. Yet lower variance would justify trimming epochs while still trusting the 40-seed mean.
critiques.suggestion: Add an H4: 'reducing per-seed accuracy variance (e.g., weight EMA, or a lower final LR at the end of the schedule) lets epochs be cut while holding the 40-seed mean >=75%'. Its prediction would be per-seed std down by >=30% at equal mean.
